text:
marco: Customer using our Windows/Electron app behind a corporate proxy — intermittent 401s. They can't find a Request ID to attach. What to ask them to send?

jess: Quick checklist to ask the customer (short):
- exact timestamp (timezone) of failure
- one failing request's raw headers (screenshot from DevTools OK)
- the X-Redwood-Request-Id / x-request-id header if present
- a minimal curl that reproduces the call (no API key) or a HAR
- console debug bundle if they can (see steps below)

marco: For non-dev customers, give these step-by-step Windows/Electron hints:
1) Open the app, go to the screen that triggers the call.
2) Press Ctrl+Shift+I to open DevTools. Click Network tab.
3) Reproduce the failure, click the failing request, open Headers.
4) Copy value of any of: `X-Redwood-Request-Id`, `x-request-id`, `x-rwd-req` — paste into the thread or screenshot.
5) If the webview is wrapped and DevTools blocked, ask them to: Menu -> Help -> Toggle Developer Tools (or run `\"app.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222\"` then attach).

marco: If headers are missing (common with proxies):
- Ask them to run Fiddler/Charles / Windows loopback capture and export the single request.
- Alternatively run this curl from their workstation (replace domain):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate --trace-ascii trace.txt
```

- Then attach trace.txt (contains the request/response, TLS handshake metadata).

ingrid: For eng triage we need:
- request id header value (preferred) OR full curl + --trace-ascii output
- the service region & model name they were hitting (if in UI/API logs)
- a screenshot of the request headers section (showing status code + time)

marco: How to generate a Console debug bundle (if customer on Hosted account):
1) Console -> Settings -> Support -> Generate debug bundle (do NOT include secrets).
2) Include the bundle name + time in the thread, or upload to our secure file share.

jess: Minimal reproducible curl to send to us (remove keys):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat
```

jess: If customer can't run commands, ask them to: DevTools -> Network -> right-click request -> Save as HAR -> attach HAR. HAR is ideal.

ingrid: If we see no request-id in our logs, common root causes: proxy stripping, CDN removing headers, or SDK not forwarding header. Ask whether they use an enterprise proxy/inspection appliance.

marco: Privacy/process note: remind them NOT to paste API keys or full auth header. They can redact `Bearer abc...` -> `Bearer <REDACTED>`. We need the rest. :lock: :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Please upload attachments to the secure escalation folder: https://files.redwood/safe-upload -> include thread_ts 3425001234. Do not post secrets in channel.

marco: Example screenshot markup we want (one-liner they can do quickly):
- Screenshot -> highlight Headers area -> highlight `x-request-id` value -> send.

jess: If customer is on Dedicated or Private: also ask them to capture the edge proxy logs for the minute around the timestamp (UTC).

marco: TL;DR (one-line for agent to paste to customer):
"Can you send a screenshot of the failing request headers (or the x-request-id value), the exact failure timestamp, a HAR or minimal curl (no API key), and a Console debug bundle if available?" :mag: :paperclip:

ingrid: Thanks — if they attach trace/curl + request-id we'll pull the trace and link to the internal span. Otherwise we'll need packet/har/proxy logs.

marco: I'll paste this to the customer now. :thumbsup:
